Summary of the most relevant privacy/regulatory points (short bullets):

- DPA / SCCs: Redwood provides a standard DPA that includes EU SCC modules for controller-to-processor transfers. We have a canonical redline attached. Where customers require alternative legal language we can negotiate — expect ~5–10 business days for legal review on non-standard clauses.

- HIPAA / BAA feasibility: Redwood will sign a BAA for customers using Dedicated or Private deployments (VPC or on-prem). For hosted (shared) deployments we can consider a BAA only in specific enterprise agreements with network and tenancy isolation guarantees; this typically requires Dedicated capacity or private tenancy plus contract terms. Operational prerequisites for BAA: (1) dedicated customer tenancy for PHI, (2) agreed retention and deletion SLOs, (3) KMS integration for CMEK to limit key access.

- SOC 2 Type II: attached snapshot covers our infra, deployment orchestration, and serving runtime; scope includes production control plane and production GPU pools used for inference. We are happy to provide a full SOC2 under NDA for in-depth review.

- Subprocessors & data flows: active subprocessors list is included in the SIG responses (Annex A). We use cloud providers for infrastructure and have contractual flow-downs. For EU data residency requests we can provide region-specific capacity and routing.

- Encryption & KMS: Data at rest is encrypted. For Dedicated/Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (CMEK) via KMS/HSM integrations; for hosted API we offer platform-managed encryption but can discuss KMIP/HSM integrations for enterprise contracts.

Next steps (proposed):
- We will deliver the annotated SIG and DPA redline (today).
- Soojin to confirm SCC module text and escalate any legal blockers.
- Karthik / Sales to confirm whether pilot requires PHI in EU or US-only.
